title: Silverpine Systems — Edge compatibility & onramp discovery

Schedule 1-hr perf benchmark with Silverpine infra team (target week of 2026-03-29)
Share integration diagram and approximate cost model (Redwood Optimize suggestions) by 2026-03-24

Priya Nair - propose perf benchmark plan + test vectors - 2026-03-26

summary: Intro call between Redwood and Silverpine to assess feasibility of integrating Redwood onramp for Silverpine's edge-GPU footprint. Key concerns: VPC peering, KMS/encryption, latency SLAs for sub-50ms tails, pilot scope and who owns OS-level drivers for edge racks. Agreed to run a small benchmark and exchange security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Coleman (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Jamie, AE on the partner motion. Priya's our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Evan Park (Silverpine CTO): Evan here. Maya and Sam from my team also on.
[00:12] Maya Lin (Partner Eng): Hi all. excited to dig in.
[00:15] Priya Nair (Redwood SE): hey, thanks. quick agenda: 1) understand Silverpine edge topology and constraints, 2) discuss integration patterns (VPC, on-prem, peering), 3) pilot framing.
[00:25] Sam Ortiz (Infra lead): sounds good. to frame — we run racks in 12 regional edge sites, each has a mix of A100-ish and some lower power T4-ish cards. latency budget for inference-heavy routes is 30 to 80ms depending on region.
[00:40] Jamie: ok great, the diversity is typical. are these in your own datacenters or colo?
[00:45] Sam: mostly colo, some customer-owned edge colo. networking varies — some sites allow full VPC, some only limited routes.
[00:50] Priya: got it. we usually surface three integration patterns: hosted (Redwood API), dedicated (reserved pools in a partner region), and private on-prem via our private control plane. for edge onramp usually we do a hybrid: routing policy + local model variants for tails.
[01:04] Maya: when you say private control plane, do you run any agent in our network? how much we need to open?
[01:08] Priya: we can do a customer-managed control plane with a small agent for routing and health checks. or a peered VPC model where requests route to a dedicated gateway in your VPC. agent footprint is small — container plus svc that does auth handshake with your KMS.
[01:22] Rhea Kapoor (Security): KMS is our big blocker. we need to keep keys in our HSM and no plaintext ever leaves our boundary. can Redwood integrate with custom HSMs?
[01:32] Jamie: yes - we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments. we'll share the KMS integration doc. note: hosted API doesn't work for that use case unless you accept bring-your-own-key via a partner gateway.
[01:46] Evan: what about SOC2 and audit logs? can't have black boxes.
[01:50] Jamie: we have SOC2 + ISO summary we can share and our console offers per-token tracing and audit logs. I'll attach the security pack.
[01:58] Sam: performance — how do you manage KV cache and batching at edge? we can't have a global cache that increases tail latencies.
[02:06] Priya: good question. for edge we recommend a per-site prefix/KV cache with local serving kernel selection. that preserves cold-start behavior but gives caching benefits. batching is workload-aware; we can run micro-batches with latency SLOs. we've seen 20-30% cost savings without hurting 95th percentile when tuned.
[02:25] Evan: any inference runtime constraints? we rely on custom CUDA drivers and mixed-precision quantized models.
[02:32] Priya: runtime supports a lot of quantization profiles. on custom drivers we can ship a slim runtime shim but we need an ops contact. some of our partners run a small compatibility test to validate kernels.
[02:45] Liam Torres (Redwood SE): note — we sometimes misrecognize vendor names on transcripts, but expected step is a driver-level smoke test.
[02:51] Maya: are you able to fall back to a cloud region if local capacity is exhausted?
[02:55] Jamie: yes — smart routing lets us route by latency or cost. fallback to a compatible model variant in another region is standard; you can define policies per-route.
[03:05] Sam: cost — how do you price dedicated capacity for partner edge?
[03:09] Jamie: two options: reserved pool pricing with monthly commit or usage-based with burst buffer. for edge partners typically a small reserved footprint plus on-demand burst into Redwood Dedicated or hosted API. we'll share ballpark numbers.
[03:20] Evan: timeline — if we wanted to pilot, what's realistic? 6–8 weeks?
[03:25] Priya: typical pilot is 4–6 weeks if you provide access to two edge sites and sample traffic. 6–8 weeks is safe if driver/install/approval cycles are longer.
[03:33] Rhea: will we need an NDA? we have partner legal requirements.
[03:36] Jamie: we can run an MSA + partner addendum; I'll start the legal thread. NDA ok too.
[03:40] Maya: ok cool, show of hands — who needs what to sign off internally?
[03:44] Evan: I need security sign-off (Rhea) and infra sign off (Sam). After that product review.
[03:48] Rhea: for security we want to see KMS HSM support, audit logs, data residency controls, and a clear ops runbook.
[03:56] Priya: we'll include a runbook draft in the pack. also propose a 2-hour deep technical workshop during the pilot planning phase.
[04:04] Sam: can we run a perf benchmark with our real models? we want to validate 95th pct tail under load.
[04:09] Priya: absolutely — we'll define bench vectors and sampling cadence. small note: sometimes transcripts flip product names — Redwood Dedicated referenced as Redwood Devoted earlier in some notes, ignore that.
[04:20] Maya: haha ok. any gotchas with OS-level driver versions across your fleet?
[04:24] Liam: mismatched drivers are the top failure mode; we recommend a driver matrix and an automated smoke test.
[04:31] Evan: competitors — we evaluated MegaCloud AI and NimbusCompute; both had lower integration overhead but higher per-token costs.
[04:40] Jamie: that's common. our value prop here is predictable latency and rollouts with an ops-focused console.
[04:46] Sam: on telemetry — can we get per-request traces and token level latencies to our Splunk?
[04:51] Priya: yes — we support exporting traces and have a Trace→Splunk pipeline; we can also add a minimal agent to ship logs.
[04:58] Rhea: retention policies? we need 90-day logs for audit.
[05:02] Jamie: retention configurable via Redwood Console add-on. we'll include options.
[05:07] Maya: ok let's recap next steps.
[05:11] Jamie: recap: 1) Redwood sends security pack + KMS/HSM notes (Jamie) 2) Redwood proposes perf benchmark plan + vectors (Priya) 3) Silverpine shares traffic profile and two edge site access details (Sam) 4) legal thread / NDA (Jamie) 5) schedule week-of 3/29 bench. agreed?
[05:31] Evan: agreed.
[05:32] Sam: agreed.
[05:34] Rhea: agreed pending KMS details.
[05:36] Jamie: great. any final q's?
[05:38] Maya: none, thanks all.
[05:40] Jamie: thanks for your time — we'll follow up with docs.
[05:42] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard terms (Redwood Devoted vs Dedicated), speaker overlaps, and dropped punctuation. Some product features referred to colloquially (e.g., "onramp") which in docs are formalized as Redwood Private or Redwood Dedicated.
